Then (u,v) lies on U²+V²=2 and u≠1 because x≠0. The rational line through (1,1) and (u,v) has finite slope t=(v−1)/(u−1). Its second intersection with the circle gives x=4t(1−t²)/(1+t²)². Writing t=m/n in lowest terms with n>0 yields the claimed expression; nonzero x forces m≠0 and m≠±n."},{"claim":"For primitive m,n satisfying the stated exclusions, the reduced denominator is r², where r=(m²+n²)/gcd(m²+n²,2); r is odd, at least 5, and each prime divisor of r is 1 modulo 4.","reasoning":"For odd p dividing q=m²+n², p divides neither m nor n. If p also divided n²−m², it would divide 2m², a contradiction; hence no odd factor of q cancels against N=4mn(n²−m²). If q is odd, there is no denominator factor 2. If q is even, coprimality makes m,n odd, q≡2 mod 8, and 8 divides n²−m²; thus v₂(N)≥5 while v₂(q²)=2, giving exactly a factor 4 of cancellation. This proves the denominator formula. Each odd p dividing r has (m/n)²≡−1 mod p, so p≡1 mod 4. For odd q, q≥5 since m,n are nonzero; for even q, r≡1 mod 4 and r=1 would force q=2 and m=±n. Thus r≥5."},{"claim":"The reduced numerator is divisible by 24.","reasoning":"If q is odd, mn is even, so 8 divides N, and no factor of q cancels from N. If q is even, 8 divides n²−m², so after the exact cancellation by 4 the reduced numerator remains divisible by 8. For divisibility by 3, either 3 divides mn or m,n are both nonzero modulo 3 and their squares agree, so 3 divides n²−m². Coprimality ensures 3 does not divide q, so this factor remains after reduction. Divisibility by both 8 and 3 gives divisibility by 24."},{"claim":"The final reformulation of the six mutual-edge conditions is valid, and the proof does not resolve the main sextuple question.","reasoning":"For reduced x_i=u_i/r_i², the edge value is (u_i u_j+r_i²r_j²)/(r_i r_j)². It is positive because each common neighbor lies strictly between −1 and 1. A positive integer divided by a positive square is a rational square exactly when that integer is an integer square. This reformulates, but does not settle, the six mutual conditions; the candidate explicitly leaves their simultaneous feasibility and the main existence question unresolved."}] }]}}
